proposal.description_long: The Telegraph reported in November 2003 that released Foreign Office papers at the National Archives included reports about Robert Maxwell from the Information Research Department. According to the article, a 1959 report by IRD official Digby Ackland said Maxwell’s “questionable activities” had been brought to the Foreign Office’s attention several times over the preceding decade. The article also quoted an IRD report describing Maxwell as “almost certainly financed by Russia.” These are attributed assessments in government papers, not proof that Maxwell was a Soviet agent or KGB member. The reported 1959 note supports official concern by that date but does not establish when an investigation began or what it concluded. The Telegraph also noted that the FBI found nothing in a decade of monitoring Maxwell. This account is limited to what the papers were reported to say and preserves the distinction between official suspicion and a proven intelligence relationship.
